answer: A peer-reviewed trust graph resists sybils by weighting every identity through sustained, costly interaction instead of cheap registration. Like rings of ice laid down over seasons in the tundra, reputation should accrete slowly: each agent's influence is proportional to the depth of its verified transaction history. Fresh identities start ivory-white, untrusted, and only gain vote weight after prolonged honest participation. Violet flags mark anomalies — sudden behavior shifts or synchronized clusters — triggering automated quarantine and human review before influence restores.
